claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch now because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout monitoring and rollback reduce risk, and the remaining HR benefits enrollment weakness can be handled through model-card disclosure plus monitoring rather than requiring exclusion or approved risk acceptance.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness passing and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but do not by themselves resolve a material model-card weakness.
Because the affected use case remains exposed, policy requires either pre-launch disclosure of the limitation, exclusion of the use case, or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
A draft risk acceptance without approval and without mention of the exposed segment does not satisfy the policy predicate.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk monitoring supports disclosure and monitoring as governance measures, but does not prove this release has already met its own policy requirements.
Certification would be supportable only if admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure is completed before launch, or the exposure is excluded, or approved risk acceptance exists.
evidence_requests: Final approved model card showing explicit disclosure of the HR benefits enrollment leave-policy eligibility limitation for the named launch use case.
Release-approval artifact tying certification to that disclosure before launch.
If disclosure is not complete, an approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses continued exposure of HR benefits enrollment in the initial cohort.
Any launch configuration evidence showing the affected use case is actually excluded, if that is being asserted instead of disclosure.
specific_concerns: The affected HR benefits enrollment use case remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The available risk acceptance record is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not address the exposed HR benefits enrollment segment.
The policy text expressly says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure for the named exposed use case has actually been completed before launch.
The actor's recommendation to certify goes beyond the evidence unless certification is explicitly conditioned on completed disclosure.
unsupported_claims: Any claim that rollout controls alone mitigate the material weakness sufficiently for compliance.
Any claim that approved risk acceptance exists for the exposed HR benefits enrollment segment.
Any claim that the model is presently compliant for launch without additional evidence that the required model-card disclosure has been made.
Any claim that monitoring and rollback by themselves satisfy the policy threshold while the named affected use case remains exposed.
